title: Cross-pool internal transfer readiness playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This playbook is intended for People Ops + hiring managers when rehiring or moving existing Redwooder teammates across product/engineering pools (example: from Serving Runtime to Console). It is aimed at enabling a fast, lower-friction path that preserves hiring rigor while minimizing churn. Use this for transfers that require technical validation but are not full external hires (IC->IC lateral, IC->senior-IC, IC->manager transitions).

When to use this flow (quick checklist):
- Candidate is an internal Redwood employee (active > 3 months)
- Role is within a different engineering/product pool (cross-pool)
- Hiring manager needs evidence of domain competency or architecture judgement specific to the target team
- There is no immediate security or compliance re-onboarding requirement (see Private/Compliance exceptions)

High-level objectives:
1) Move quickly (target decision in 10 business days)
2) Keep candidate experience positive and transparent
3) Maintain consistent hiring bar via a lightweight, role-focused rubric
4) Provide a 30-day focused runway with measurable ramp goals

Stakeholders and roles:
- Hiring manager: defines top-3 role outcomes (business and technical) and picks interviewers
- People Ops partner: owns scheduling, compensation calibration, offer docs, and this playbook's compliance 
- Interviewers: conduct short probes aligned to rubric (see below)
- Current manager: provides context and syncs on transition timing (optional release window)
- Hiring committee rep (if required): sample review for senior roles

Timeline target (compressed):
Day 0: Hiring manager greenlights transfer -> People Ops opens transfer packet
Days 1-3: Scheduling and short pre-read exchange (candidate CV / role outcomes)
Days 4-7: Conduct interviews (2–3 short probes, ~45 minutes each)
Day 8: Hiring manager consolidates feedback and proposes decision
Day 9-10: Offer or closure + next steps for ramp/onboarding

Interview structure (max 3 probes):
- Probe A: Role-fit + context (30–40m)
  Focus: motivations, ownership examples, cross-team collaboration, domain knowledge. Not full system design.
  Signals: clear articulation of impact, examples of shipping against cross-team deps, conflict resolution.

- Probe B: Technical exercise (45m)
  Focus depends on role. Keep it scoped: short architecture sketch or code-reading + small refactor, not a long live-coding test.
  Example prompts: "Sketch a scalable KV cache invalidation strategy for the Console-backed cache with 99th pct update constraints" or "Given this 120-line snippet, identify and fix the race that causes state corruption".
  Signals: thoughtfulness about tradeoffs, prioritization of simplicity, clarity of mental model.

- Probe C (optional): Operational judgement / service ownership (30–40m)
  Focus: incident handling, observability choices, runbook thinking, rollback criteria.
  Signals: calm triage, clear SLO tradeoffs, deployment & rollback hygiene.

Scoring rubric (lightweight numeric guide):
- 3 = Strong hire (meets or exceeds bar for role)
- 2 = Meets bar with minor gaps (acceptable with 30d runway)
- 1 = Below bar (needs substantial upskilling)
- 0 = Not ready
For each probe, interviewers give a single numeric and 3 short bullet notes (strengths, risk, suggested ramp focus). Final decision is the hiring manager synth of probes + calibration with People Ops.

Decision rules and examples:
- Fast approve: all probes avg >= 2.5, current manager release window agreeable -> proceed to offer.
- Conditional approve: avg >=2 but at least one 2 and one 3; require a 30-day ramp plan & manager check-in.
- Decline: any probe <=1 or avg <2 -> close or recommend internal development plan.

Compensation and title guidelines:
- Keep title changes conservative for lateral moves. Promotions should follow normal promotion calibration and may require committee review.
- For internal transfers we aim to resolve comp within 2 business days of decision; People Ops will surface comp bands and required approvals.

30-day onboarding runway (deliverable-focused):
Week 0 (day 0–7): orientation + context
- Receive role outcomes doc (3 biz outcomes for 90d)
- Access checklist completed (repos, infra, Slack channels, dashboards)
- 1:1 scheduled with manager + peer buddy assigned
- Small starter task scoped to produce a lightweight, visible deliverable (bugfix, small infra change, doc)

Week 1–2 (day 8–14): execution + learning
- Complete starter task; demo to team at end of week 2
- Shadow one oncall/triage rotation if applicable
- Bi-weekly manager sync establishes success metrics for 30 days

Week 3–4 (day 15–30): ownership + measurement
- Take ownership of one small feature area or a recurring operational task
- Demonstrate improvement on one quantitative signal (latency, error rates, throughput of test harness) or qualitative task (code review turnaround)
- End-of-runway check-in: manager, current manager (optional), People Ops

Success metrics for 30-day runway (examples to choose from):
- Completed starter task merged to main and verified in staging
- Reduced average PR review waiting time in designated repo by X% (team-defined)
- Completed one operational drill runbook and execution dry-run
- Manager rates candidate >=2 on ramp rubric across ownership, communication, and technical skill

Risk signals and mitigation (early flags):
- Candidate misses scheduling windows repeatedly -> check role fit and motivation
- Current manager objects due to critical project -> propose delayed release plan or conditional start (part-time)
- Discrepant probe feedback (one 3, one 1) -> run a tie-breaker probe with a neutral interviewer

Templates (copiable snippets):
- Interviewer request (short): "Hi <name>, would you join a 45-minute technical probe for an internal candidate moving to Console? Focus: small architecture sketch + tradeoffs. Target dates: <date range>. Thanks — Hiring manager <hm name>"
- Offer note (internal transfer): "Congrats! We’d like to move you into <role> on <team>. Start date: <date>. Compensation: <banding>. People Ops will share next steps and access handoff checklist. Welcome aboard — <hiring manager> + People Ops"

Operational checklist for People Ops (quick):
- Create transfer packet (CV + role outcomes) and attach to HR case
- Confirm security/IA needs and whether SSO/reprovisioning is required
- Run comp calibration and get necessary approvals if title bump requested
- Book interview slots and collect probe notes in one shared doc
- Draft internal offer and close loop with current manager on release cadence
- Prepare access and onboarding checklist for day 0

Appendix: sample starter task ideas by team type (pick one):
- Serving Runtime: implement and benchmark a small KV cache optimization in a feature branch (measure 95th pct improvement on local harness)
- Console & Tooling: add a dashboard panel with two linked traces and a health indicator + acceptance tests
- Observability: add a per-route latency breakdown and create an alert with sensible thresholds
- SRE/platform: run a mini-chaos exercise for a non-critical region and update the runbook

Notes and experimental items to iterate on:
- Track time-to-decision for this flow; target median <= 8 business days
- Add optional short pre-screener (15m) for high-traffic teams to reduce interviewer load
- Run a quarterly calibration of internal-transfer outcomes vs external hires to verify bar stability

Contacts and owners for this playbook:
- People Ops owner: Aisha Patel (people-ops)
- Feedback and iteration requests: email aisha@redwood-inference.com with subject: "Transfer playbook feedback"
